basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A mixin that adds support for an existing assertion: evidence items, warrant, assumptions and counter-evidence.
Differs from provenance, which tracks origin; this model argues why a conclusion is justified.
Differs from a citation record, which identifies sources but not how they support a claim.
Records custody, sealing and certainty appraisal of the evidence body.

may: Attach evidence to a claim or decision with a typed support relation.
Anchor an excerpt to the exact location in its source.
Register counter-evidence and record how it was resolved.
Produce a redacted disclosure copy for an authorized requester.
mustNot: Fabricate or paraphrase evidence and present it as a quotation.
Claim sufficiency without assessing against the decision threshold.
Break chain of custody by altering sealed items.
Disclose evidence containing personal data beyond the declared audience.
requiresHuman: Judging sufficiency for a legal, clinical or safety decision.

considerations: People can be harmed by decisions based on weak or selectively presented evidence.
Evidence often contains personal data about third parties.
Agents must not make generated text look like source evidence.
affectedParties: People affected by the supported decision
Authors and subjects of evidence items

items: A support record links an assertion to evidence items with relation types, warrant and certainty.
Often confused with a bibliography, an audit log and an attachment folder.
Cherry-picked evidence leads to unjust decisions.
W3C Web Annotation Data Model for anchoring excerpts.
GRADE approach for certainty of evidence.
